metadata.case_name: CHOY FOR SANG v. TONG KWOK MING

source: arteriography was performed which revealed an intracranial haematoma.

injuries.description: 5 lacerations of his face measuring from 2 c.m. to 6 c.m.
source: taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in an unconscious state with 5 lacerations of his face measuring from 2 c.m. to 6 c.m. and multiple abrasions of the forearms.

injuries.description: injury to his upper jaw which resulted in the replacing of a number of teeth
source: it is plain that the Plaintiff also suffered injury to his upper jaw which resulted in the replacing of a number of teeth.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of teeth or supporting structures

source: taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in an unconscious state with 5 lacerations of his face measuring from 2 c.m. to 6 c.m. and multiple abrasions of the forearms.

manifestations.description: severe double vision in all gaze positions except looking up to the left.
greatest difficulty in doing anything or going anywhere. His activities are almost completely curtailed.

treatments_received: taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in an unconscious state
on 22nd June, the Plaintiff underwent a craniotomy to remove the haematoma
placed in the intensive care unit
replacing of a number of teeth
treatments_future: lengthy and complex surgery and treatment required to afford some measure of correction to his double vision
the course of treatment would last about 12 months and take 2 or 3 operations
recommended that the Plaintiff should go to London or Australia where there are special clinics dealing with eye problems

losses.description: severe double vision in all gaze positions except looking up to the left.
greatest difficulty in doing anything or going anywhere. His activities are almost completely curtailed.
unfit for any employment; total loss of earnings for at least another 12 months; permanent reduction of earnings likely of not less than $500 per month.

comparable_cases.injury_description: double vision; vision had returned very nearly to normal and there was no loss of earnings
double vision; the injured person was able to do copy typing and the degree of disability appears to have been comparable with the instant case
